data.G: Initial G remains the measured baseline (commit 9edc22c4ee0b2af92510de44fe714d5ac17bb086). Defer integration until the research trees return measured, correct candidates; then compare any combinations directly and independently confirm the selected final program.
data.analysis: Choose N=2. The supplied source recursively launches reduce0 for each level: at n=4194304 and 128 threads per block, that is four reduction kernels, followed by a device-to-device copy. Each block reduction uses shared memory, repeated CTA synchronization, and a modulo-based active-thread predicate. The valid baseline measured 46.4832 microseconds on average across three samples (score 0.5); this is a whole-call reference, not evidence attributing time to a particular cost. The two trees target complementary dimensions: global reduction topology and per-block reduction cost. A separate load-vectorization tree would overlap with choosing the global tile geometry, while a small-input-only tree does not directly target the stated performance size. Preserve exactness for all valid inputs: a true total that fits int32 does not imply every arbitrary intermediate sub-sum fits int32, so bound intermediate groups safely or use int64 accumulation and narrow only after the exact total is known. Respect scratch capacity, its uninitialized state, and the existing launch and allocation constraints. Reserve time for direct comparisons and independent confirmation; do not assume improvements compose.

children.objective: Explore a generic hierarchical reduction topology that reduces global passes for large inputs. Aim to read the input once into partial sums and finish on device with fewer launches than the baseline's recursive four-kernel path at the performance size; tune CTA tile size and the final partial-sum reduction based on measured full-call latency. Handle other valid n values generically, use only the supplied scratch and default stream, and never rely on scratch initialization or a one-CTA scan of the entire large input. Preserve exactness under cancellation: ensure partial sums cannot overflow, for example with int64 intermediates, and narrow only after the true total is established. Validate all required inputs, compare against the measured baseline, and report failed variants and repeated measurements.
children.subject: Global reduction topology and launch count

children.objective: Explore replacing reduce0's intra-block modulo/shared-memory reduction tree with a lower-synchronization block reduction, such as warp shuffles plus a small shared warp-partial exchange or an allowed CUB block primitive. To isolate this axis, retain the baseline's recursive global pass structure, 128-thread mapping, and one input element per lane; do not change the global tile geometry. Preserve correct synchronization and exact summation for every valid input, including safe handling of intermediate sums, and obey the scratch, stream, allocation, and bounds constraints. Validate all required inputs and compare repeated full-call measurements against the baseline; report failures and do not assume a local-kernel improvement guarantees a whole-call improvement.
